risks.risk: Leakage or seepage at the lid seal/gasket or around seams/bottom that photos cannot confirm.
risks.proof: Ask for a short video of the drum filled with water (or a pressure/soak test) showing no dripping over 30–60 minutes, plus a close-up of the lid seal area.
risks.if_unproven: Price as potentially needing seal replacement / not guaranteed leak-free (worst case: treat as not confirmed leak-free).

risks.risk: Not actually food-grade (previous chemical/industrial use) despite the seller’s statement.
risks.proof: Ask for any visible food-grade certification/label details (clear close-up of markings) and/or a document/receipt; also request a photo of the inside wall after rinsing.
risks.if_unproven: Price as general-purpose storage drum (worst case: not food-grade).

risks.risk: Hidden cracks or damage near the bottom curvature, around mounting points, or under scuffed areas.
risks.proof: Request close-up photos of: (1) bottom, (2) lid rim and gasket seat, (3) any dents/scuffed spots, and (4) side seams—taken in good light.
risks.if_unproven: Price as used with possible cosmetic/structural wear (worst case: assume damage may exist).

risks.risk: Capacity/size uncertainty (price depends heavily on volume).
risks.proof: Ask for the drum capacity marking (liters/gallons) or a tape-measure photo (height and diameter) and the exact number of drums.
risks.if_unproven: Price at the smallest likely size among common options, or treat as unknown-size until confirmed.

proof_requests: Clear close-up of the lid rim and gasket/seat (showing condition).
Video or photos of a leak test (fill with water and show no dripping for 30–60 minutes).
Close-up of any markings/certifications on the drum (food-grade/NSF or equivalent) and inside-wall photo after rinsing.
Capacity confirmation: photo of the liters/gallons label or provide height + diameter measurements.
Confirm the exact quantity available for sale (how many drums).
response.reason: The item type is clear (plastic liquid storage drums with lids), but key pricing drivers—food-grade status, leak-free condition, and exact capacity—cannot be verified from the current photos. Until leak test and capacity/markings are provided, it must be priced at worst-case assumptions, so proof is needed to price confidently.
